title: The app sometimes forgets (disable) certain features that users have enabled (for example, lightswitch)

judgment.rationale: The report establishes that an enabled feature can later appear disabled and includes a diagnostic archive, but the latest discussion has not established whether the behavior recurs on the current stable build or whether the state loss affects only LightSwitch. The available code points to settings/module initialization as plausible areas, not a confirmed root cause.
evidence: The reporter says PowerToys 0.101.2362 sometimes disables LightSwitch without user action.
Automated triage found no matching crash or error signature in the diagnostic subset and suggested a silent persistence or initialization problem with medium confidence.
A maintainer asked whether the behavior is random or occurs after upgrading, and that question is unanswered.
judgment.recommended_action: Request confirmation of recurrence and scope on the current stable build, then use the result to decide whether to investigate LightSwitch state persistence or a broader module-enable/settings path.

fix_assessment.rationale: A repository fix is applicable, but the current evidence does not distinguish a LightSwitch settings persistence problem from a broader settings or module initialization problem.

proposed_fixes.title: Preserve enabled-module state across reload and startup
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: a settings reload, migration, or module initialization path can write or consume an incomplete enabled-state snapshot, causing an enabled LightSwitch entry to be treated as disabled.
plan: Trace the LightSwitch settings read/write and the general enabled-module state through startup and settings-change notifications.
Compare the persisted enabled state with the module's runtime initialization state after an observed disable event.
Ensure state reload and migration preserve an explicitly enabled module and add regression coverage for restart and settings-change boundaries.
verification: On the affected stable build, reproduce the state loss and capture the time and whether any other module changes state.
After the owning path is identified, restart PowerToys and toggle unrelated settings repeatedly; verify LightSwitch remains enabled and its persisted state is unchanged.

confidence.rationale: The symptom and the LightSwitch/general-settings ownership fit a persistence or initialization defect, but the diagnostic subset showed no direct failure and the discussion does not yet identify the triggering transition.

issue_context.summary: The reporter observes that an enabled LightSwitch feature sometimes becomes disabled without an intentional change. A diagnostic archive was supplied, but the latest maintainer question about upgrade dependence and recurrence remains unanswered.
known_information: PowerToys version reported was 0.101.2362 on Windows build 26200.
The installation is per-user, non-elevated, and from GitHub.
The report names LightSwitch and General, and the expected state is that an enabled feature remains enabled.
A PowerToys diagnostic ZIP is attached to the issue.
Automated triage found no matching crash or error signature in its sanitized diagnostic subset.
inferences: The behavior may involve state persistence or module initialization rather than an exception-driven crash, but this is not confirmed.
If multiple enabled modules change together, the general settings path is more likely than a LightSwitch-only scheduler defect.
issue_context.analysis: The issue is actionable only after one targeted clarification because the report mixes a module-specific example with a general claim about features being disabled. The repository has distinct LightSwitch settings/state code and a general enabled-module path, so the maintainer needs the recurrence and scope details to select the correct investigation boundary.
initial_investigation: LightSwitch settings are represented in Settings.UI.Library and consumed by LightSwitchService state management, including reloads on settings changes.
LightSwitchStateManager reloads module settings before evaluating and applying the theme, making settings reload and persisted values relevant ownership points.
The issue's automated diagnostic summary did not identify a direct exception or crash signature.
No linked fix or duplicate was provided in the issue discussion.

information_gaps.information: Whether the behavior still reproduces on the current stable build after the reporter's latest update, and the approximate time or trigger when it happens.
information_gaps.why_needed: This distinguishes an upgrade-specific regression from an ongoing state-loss defect and provides a correlation point for logs.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Use the current stable build, note the last time LightSwitch was confirmed enabled, and record the approximate time it becomes disabled.

information_gaps.information: Whether only LightSwitch is disabled or other enabled PowerToys features change state at the same time.
information_gaps.why_needed: This separates a LightSwitch-specific path from general enabled-module/settings persistence.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: After the next occurrence, compare the affected module list in Settings and submit a fresh /bugreport immediately after reproducing.

actions.label: Confirm LightSwitch state loss
actions.note: Ask for the two issue-specific facts that determine whether to investigate LightSwitch or general settings persistence.

comment.body:
Thanks for the report and for attaching the diagnostic ZIP. The report confirms that LightSwitch can appear disabled without an intentional change, but the current discussion does not yet show whether this still reproduces on the current stable build or whether other PowerToys features change state with it. Please provide:

1. Whether it reproduces after your latest update, including the approximate time or trigger.
2. Whether only LightSwitch is disabled or other enabled features change too.

After the next occurrence, please compare the affected module list in Settings and submit a fresh /bugreport immediately so the logs cover the failure window.

actions.label: Design fix for enabled-state persistence
actions.note: Approve a focused investigation of LightSwitch and general enabled-module state persistence after the requested evidence narrows the ownership boundary.
